name: AltarDesk
shortDescription: A UK system for church members, giving and Gift Aid, rotas and messages. It also covers governance, pastoral appointments and safeguarding administration.
suitableContexts: UK churches seeking one platform for people records, giving, rotas and governance
Churches that need documented UK Gift Aid and data-processing information
Multi-site churches needing named permission and administration controls

pricing.summary: AltarDesk publishes VAT-inclusive monthly plans from £17 for up to 75 members through £99 for up to 1,000 members, plus a custom annual plan for larger organisations. Monthly and annual plans are stated to have no lock-in; annual billing saves two months.

startingPrice.qualifier: Starter plan for up to 75 members, including VAT

tiers.label: Starter
tiers.detail: Up to 75 members, member app, email, Gift Aid management, rotas and reports

tiers.label: Standard
tiers.detail: Up to 200 members; adds safeguarding, HMRC claim submission and more administration

tiers.label: Pro
tiers.detail: Up to 500 members; adds multi-site tools and custom admin groups

pricing.trialDetails: Every new account starts on a 30-day Pro trial without a payment card, according to the supplier.

dataHosting: The supplier's data-processing agreement states that primary application hosting is in the United Kingdom and database, authentication and file storage are in the European Economic Area. The agreement lists transfer safeguards for relevant US sub-processors.
gdprInformation: AltarDesk publishes a data-processing agreement identifying the church as controller and Rayscent as processor, with a named sub-processor list, security measures and transfer information. This is supplier information, not a compliance determination for a church.
coreFeatures: Gift Aid, GASDS and donation tracking
Sermon and media hub using the church's Google Drive
integrations: Stripe Payments UK for online donations
Google Drive for sermon and media files
The SMS Works for SMS delivery
importExport: Full data export is listed across plans
Google Drive keeps sermon and media files in the church's own storage
support: Phone and priority support from Pro
Dedicated onboarding on Pro and above

uk-purchasing.value: Rayscent Ltd is registered in England and Wales; sterling, VAT-inclusive plans are published.

gbp-pricing.value: Published plans range from £17 to £99 per month including VAT, plus a custom annual plan.

gift-aid.value: Supplier documents Gift Aid and GASDS management on every plan, with direct HMRC claim submission from Standard upwards.

data-processing.value: A current DPA names controller and processor roles, sub-processors and international-transfer safeguards.

hosting.value: Supplier DPA identifies primary application hosting in the UK and database, authentication and file storage in the EEA.

exports.value: Supplier documents CSV, print and full data export; sermon and media files use the church's own Google Drive.

role-permissions.value: Supplier describes per-user permissions, row-level organisation isolation and restricted safeguarding records.

audit-logs.value: Supplier DPA describes administrative-access logs; product material describes an append-only sensitive-action log.

editorial.assessment: AltarDesk is a newer UK all-in-one contender with unusually detailed published pricing and data-processing documentation. Its breadth can simplify a church's stack, but the broadest workflows—Gift Aid, safeguarding, finance controls, pastoral records and Google Drive media—should be tested by their actual owners before a migration decision.
bestFor: UK churches wanting people, giving, rotas and communications in one product
Teams that need public documentation about UK pricing, processing roles and exports
Growing or multi-site churches that need structured admin groups and permissions
strengths: Published GBP, VAT-inclusive plans and a 30-day trial
Detailed public DPA includes sub-processors, processing roles and transfer safeguards
Gift Aid, rotas, safeguarding, governance and media storage are documented in one platform
limitations: The supplier is newly incorporated, so long-term operational track record still needs independent assessment
Supplier documentation remains a supplier claim, not a certification of a church's compliance or financial controls
The church must separately govern sensitive pastoral and safeguarding information and its Google Drive access

procurementVerdict.problem: UK churches seeking a documented all-in-one administration platform
procurementVerdict.differentiator: Broad church workflows are paired with unusually specific published pricing and data-processing information
procurementVerdict.firstCheck: Run a role-led trial of exports, Gift Aid, permissions, safeguarding boundaries, finance approval and Google Drive ownership
